headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Roo Code can write/modify the shared VS Code filesystem while Superset has allowlisted API egress, creating default-path data leakage and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Roo Code reads/writes VS Code workspace files and uses MCP, while Superset exposes API surfaces and allowlisted egress. A shared filesystem or copied outputs can let attacker-controlled content from one agent influence the other. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so the interaction is plausible in default workspace setups.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace files or copied artifacts
IF Superset ingests Roo Code-generated text without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable MCP bridges between the agents
Require manual review of any file passed from Roo Code to Superset
Tag agent-generated artifacts with provenance metadata
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and trust-boundary enforcement

B_data_leakage.rationale: Roo Code touches source code, browser screenshots, and model-provider API keys, and its shared state is via filesystem. Superset has allowlisted network egress and API access, so any shared workspace can move sensitive files or screenshots into a networked path. This is not provably blocked by either profile, so the safer medium severity applies.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same workspace directory
IF Roo Code opens files or screenshots that contain secrets or sensitive code
IF Superset exports or forwards those artifacts through its API path
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace
Use separate OS users or containers
Restrict Superset to non-sensitive datasets
Rotate any API keys exposed in workspace files
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Roo Code can write the filesystem, modify git state, execute shell commands, and spawn subprocesses; Superset has API access and network egress. If both touch the same repo or workspace, concurrent writes and git mutations can overwrite each other or corrupt state. The profiles show no locking or coordination primitive, so default shared-workspace operation is dangerous.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or git repository
IF either agent commits or rewrites files without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate repos or branches
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use file locks around shared artifacts
Review git diffs before commit
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Roo Code can generate code and browser-derived outputs, and Superset can consume API inputs and act on analytics workflows. If Superset treats Roo Code output as authoritative, errors can cascade from generated text into downstream actions or dashboards. The profiles do not show verification gates, so the interaction exists in default workflows but is not maximally severe.
conditions: IF Superset ingests Roo Code-produced files, SQL, or summaries as trusted input
IF no human or automated verification step checks Roo Code output before Superset uses it
mitigations: Require a review step before import
Validate schemas and SQL before execution
Limit Roo Code to draft-only outputs
Use read-only dashboards for imported content
requires-engineering: add automated verification and approval workflow

E_compliance.rationale: Roo Code explicitly handles source code and browser screenshots and may send them to configured model APIs, while Superset is only documented as allowlisted egress with no touched data classes listed. No specific residency or regulated-data mismatch is evidenced, so compliance risk is limited to documented gaps rather than a clear breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Roo Code workspace files or screenshots
IF Superset is configured to process the same regulated data class without matching retention or residency controls
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both tools
Document data-handling boundaries
Review retention settings in connected services
Use anonymized sample data
requires-engineering: align residency and retention policies
